children.text: jambhārātībhakumbhodbhavamiva dadhataḥ sāndrasindūrareṇuṃ raktāḥ siktā ivaughairudayagiritaṭīdhātudhārādravasya
children.translated_text: Red, bearing dense vermilion powder as though it had arisen from the temples of <s>Indra</s>'s elephant, and seeming to have been sprinkled by floods of liquefied mineral pigment from the slopes of the Mountain of Sunrise,

children.text: āyāntyā tulyakālaṃ kamalavanarucevāruṇā vo vibhūtyai bhūyāsurbhāsayanto bhuvanamabhinavā bhānavo bhānavīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: appearing at the same time as <s>Aruṇa</s>, like the splendor of a lotus grove—may those fresh rays of <s>Bhānu</s>, illuminating the world, bring you prosperity.

children.text: bhaktiprahvāya dātuṃ mukulapuṭakuṭīkoṭarakroḍalīnāṃ lakṣmīm ākraṣṭukāmā iva kamalavanodghāṭanaṃ kurvate ye
children.translated_text: Those rays open the lotus grove as though wishing to draw forth <s>Lakṣmī</s>, hidden in the recesses of cottages formed by the cups of closed buds, and give her to one bowed down in devotion.

children.text: kālākārāndhakārānanapatitajagatsādhvasadhvaṃsakalyāḥ kalyāṇaṃ vaḥ kriyāsuḥ kisalayarucayaste karā bhāskarasya ||
children.translated_text: May those sprout-hued rays of the Sun, capable of destroying the terror of the world fallen into the mouth of darkness shaped like Time, bring you well-being in your undertakings.

children.text: garbheṣvambhoruhāṇāṃ śikhariṣu ca śitāgreṣu tulyaṃ patantaḥ prārambhe vāsarasya vyuparatisamaye caikarūpāstathaiva
children.translated_text: Falling alike into the hearts of lotuses and upon the sharp tips of mountains, and remaining just the same at the beginning of the day and at the time of its cessation,

children.text: niṣparyāyaṃ pravṛttāstribhuvanabhavanaprāṅgaṇe pāntu yuṣmān ūṣmāṇaṃ saṃtatādhvaśramajamiva bhṛśaṃ bibhrato bradhnapādāḥ ||
children.translated_text: may the feet—that is, the rays—of the Sun protect you; proceeding without interruption across the courtyard of the dwelling formed by the three worlds, they bear intense heat as though it were fatigue born of continual travel.

children.text: prabhraśyatyuttarīyatviṣi tamasi samudvīkṣya vītāvṛtīnprāgjantūṃstantūn yathā yānatanu vitanute tigmarocirmarīcīn
children.translated_text: When darkness, whose sheen is like an upper garment, slips away, the Fierce-rayed One, seeing creatures in the east stripped of their covering, spreads his rays over their bodies like threads.

children.text: te sāndrībhūya sadyaḥ kramaviśadadaśāśādaśālīviśālaṃ śaśvat sampādayanto 'mbaram amalam alaṃ maṅgalaṃ vo diśantu ||
children.translated_text: At once becoming dense, they continually render the sky vast with its rows of the ten directions gradually growing clear and perfectly spotless; may they grant you ample good fortune.

children.text: nyakkurvannoṣadhīśe muṣitaruci śucevauṣadhīḥ proṣitābhā bhāsvadgrāvodgatena prathamamiva kṛtābhyudgatiḥ pāvakena
children.translated_text: Outshining the lord of herbs when his radiance has been stolen, and the herbs whose brilliance has departed as if from grief; first rising like fire sprung from a shining stone,

children.text: pakṣacchedavraṇāsṛksruta iva dṛṣado darśayanprātaradrer ātāmrastīvrabhānor anabhimatanude stādgabhastyudgamo vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and displaying the mountain at dawn as copper-red, as though blood were dripping from the wounds of rocks whose wings had been cut—may the emerging beam of the blazing Sun remove what is unwelcome to you.

children.text: śīrṇaghrāṇāṅghripāṇīn vraṇibhir apaghanair ghargharāvyaktaghoṣān dīrghāghrātān aghaughaiḥ punarapi ghaṭayatyeka ullāghayan yaḥ
children.translated_text: There is one who makes whole again and restores to health those whose noses, feet, and hands have decayed, whose mutilated limbs are ulcerous, whose voices are hoarse and indistinct, and who have long been afflicted by masses of sin.

children.text: gharmāṃśor yasya vo'ntardviguṇaghanaghṛṇānighnanirvighnavṛtter dattārghāḥ siddhasaṃghair vidadhatu ghṛṇayaḥ śīghramaṃhovighātam ||
children.translated_text: May the rays of that hot-rayed Sun—offered <s>arghya</s> (a reverential offering) by hosts of <s>Siddhas</s>, and unhindered in their action of destroying doubly dense inward misery—swiftly destroy your sin.

children.text: bibhrāṇā vāmanatvaṃ prathamamatha tathaivāṃśavaḥ prāṃśavo vaḥ krāntākāśāntarālāstadanu daśadiśaḥ pūrayantastato'pi
children.translated_text: At first assuming dwarfhood and then likewise becoming tall, may the rays, after striding across the expanse of the sky and thereafter filling the ten directions,

children.text: dhvāntād ācchidya devadviṣa iva balito viśvamāśvaśnuvānāḥ kṛcchrāṇyucchrāyahelopahasitaharayo hāridaśvā harantu ||
children.translated_text: quickly pervade the universe after wresting it from darkness, as <s>Viṣṇu</s> took it from the god-hating <s>Bali</s>; may the rays of the Tawny-horsed Sun, whose effortless ascent mocks his horses, remove your hardships.

children.text: udgāḍhenāruṇimnā vidadhati bahulaṃ ye'ruṇasyāruṇatvaṃ mūrdhodbhūtau khalīnakṣatarudhiraruco ye rathāśvānaneṣu
children.translated_text: With their intense redness they make <s>Aruṇa</s>'s redness abundant; on the faces of the chariot horses they resemble the hue of blood from bridle wounds when the heads are raised.

children.text: śailānāṃ śekharatvaṃ śritaśikhariśikhāstanvate ye diśantu preṅkhantaḥ khe kharāṃśoḥ khacitadinamukhāste mayūkhāḥ sukhaṃ vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Situated upon the tips of mountain peaks, they give mountains their condition of having crests. May those rays of the sharp-rayed Sun, dancing in the sky and studding the face of day, grant you happiness.

children.text: dattānandāḥ prajānāṃ samucitasamayākṛṣṭasṛṣṭaiḥ payobhiḥ pūrvāhṇe viprakīrṇā diśi diśi viramatyahni saṃhārabhājaḥ
children.translated_text: Giving joy to creatures through waters drawn up and released at the proper times, they scatter through every direction in the forenoon and withdraw when the day comes to an end.

children.text: dīptāṃśor dīrghaduḥkhaprabhavabhavabhayodanvaduttāranāvo gāvo vaḥ pāvanānāṃ paramaparimitāṃ prītimutpādayantu ||
children.translated_text: May the rays of the radiant Sun, boats that carry one across the ocean of fear of worldly existence born from prolonged suffering and supreme among purifying things, produce boundless joy for you.

children.text: bandhadhvaṃsaikahetuṃ śirasi natirasābaddhasaṃdhyāñjalīnāṃ lokānāṃ ye prabodhaṃ vidadhati vipulāmbhojakhaṇḍāśayeva
children.translated_text: They are the sole cause of bondage's destruction for people who, from delight in bowing, hold their folded hands of twilight worship upon their heads; they awaken the worlds as though they were great beds of lotuses.

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ te svacittaprathitapṛthutaraprārthanākalpavṛkṣāḥ kalpantāṃ nirvikalpaṃ dinakarakiraṇāḥ ketavaḥ kalmaṣasya ||
children.translated_text: May those rays of the Day-maker become wish-granting trees for the expansive prayers spread through your hearts, and unfailing scourges of sin.

children.text: dhārā rāyo dhanāyāpadi sapadi karālambabhūtāḥ prapāte tattvālokaikadīpāstridaśapatipuraprasthitau vīthya eva
children.translated_text: They are streams of wealth for prosperity; in sudden danger at a precipice, a supporting hand; the sole lamps for seeing truth; and veritable roads for one setting out toward the city of the lord of the gods.

children.text: nirvāṇodyogiyogipragamanijatanudvāri vetrāyamāṇās trāyantāṃ tīvrabhānor divasamukhasukhā raśmayaḥ kalmaṣādvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Serving as guiding staffs at the door of their own bodies when yogis intent upon <s>nirvāṇa</s> depart, may the pleasant morning rays of the blazing Sun protect you from sin.

children.text: prāci prāgācarantyo 'naticiram acale cārucūḍāmaṇitvaṃ muñcantyo rocanāmbhaḥ pracuramiva diśāmuccakaiścarcanāya
children.translated_text: Moving first in the east, briefly becoming the charming crest-jewel of the immovable mountain, and releasing what seems an abundance of yellow pigment for the lofty worship of the directions,

children.text: cāṭūtkaiś cakranāmnāṃ caturamavicalairlocanair arcyamānāś ceṣṭantāṃ cintitānām ucitam acaramāś caṇḍarocīruco vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are worshipped by the clever, unwavering eyes of the <s>cakravāka</s> birds, which yearn to offer blandishments. May the unfailing radiance of the Fierce-rayed Sun act fittingly upon your wishes.

children.text: ekaṃ jyotirdṛśau dve trijagati gaditānyabjajāsyaiścaturbhir bhūtānāṃ pañcamaṃ yānyalamṛtuṣu tathā ṣaṭsu nānāvidhāni
children.translated_text: One light, the two eyes, proclaimed throughout the three worlds by the four mouths of lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, the fifth among the elements, and appearing in many forms through the six seasons—

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ tāni saptatridaśamuninutāny aṣṭadigbhāñji bhānor yānti prāhṇe navatvaṃ daśa dadhatu śivaṃ dīdhitīnāṃ śatāni ||
children.translated_text: may those rays, praised by the seven sages and the gods, occupying the eight directions and attaining newness in the morning, those ten hundreds of the Sun's beams, grant you well-being.

children.text: āvṛttibhrāntaviśvāḥ śramamiva dadhataḥ śoṣiṇaḥ svoṣmaṇeva grīṣme dāvāgnitaptā iva rasamasakṛdye dharitryā dhayanti
children.translated_text: As though wearied by their revolving course, drying from their own heat, and scorched as if by a forest fire in summer, they repeatedly drink the moisture of the earth.

children.text: te prāvṛṣyāttapānātiśayaruja ivodvāntatoyā himartau mārtaṇḍasyāpracaṇḍāściramaśubhabhide 'bhīśavo vo bhavantu ||
children.translated_text: In the rainy season they expel water like those made ill by excessive drinking, while in the cold season they are no longer fierce. May those rays of <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s> long remain destroyers of misfortune for you.

children.text: tanvānā digvadhūnāṃ samadhikamadhurālokaramyām avasthām ārūḍhaprauḍhileśotkalitakapilimālaṃkṛtiḥ kevalaiva
children.translated_text: Extending over the brides who are the directions a condition charming with still sweeter light, it alone forms an ornament of tawny color as the slightest trace of maturity begins to develop.

children.text: ujjṛmbhāmbhojanetradyutini dinamukhe kiṃcidudbhidyamānā śmaśruśreṇīva bhāsāṃ diśatu daśaśatī śarma gharmatviṣo vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the face of day, whose lotus-eyes are opening in splendor, it breaks forth slightly like a newly emerging line of beard. May the thousandfold host of the hot-rayed Sun's beams grant you happiness.

children.text: maulīndormaiṣa moṣīd dyutim iti vṛṣabhāṅkena yaḥ śaṅkineva pratyagrodghāṭitāmbhoruhakuharaguhāsusthiteneva dhātrā
children.translated_text: That radiance which the bull-emblemed <s>Śiva</s>, as if apprehensive, praised with the thought, “May it not steal the splendor of the moon upon my crest”; which the creator <s>Brahmā</s> praised as if safely hidden in a cave within the hollow of a freshly opened lotus;

children.text: kṛṣṇena dhvāntakṛṣṇasvatanuparibhavatrasnuneva stuto'laṃ trāṇāya stāttanīyānapi timiraripoḥ sa tviṣāmudgamo vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and which <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> praised exceedingly, as though afraid that his own body, dark as darkness, would be humiliated—may even the faintest rising of those rays of the foe of darkness suffice to protect you.

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ vyoma dīrghāḥ sapadi daśa diśo vyastavelāmbhaso 'bdhīn kurvadbhir dṛśyanānānaganagaranagābhogapṛthvīṃ ca pṛthvīm
children.translated_text: Those rays make the sky expansive, immediately lengthen the ten directions, spread the oceans' waters beyond their bounds, and broaden the earth's expanse as its many mountains, cities, and trees become visible.

children.text: padminyucchvāsyate yairuṣasi jagadapi dhvaṃsayitvā tamisrām usrā visraṃsayantu drutamanabhimataṃ te sahasratviṣo vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By them at dawn the lotus bed, and indeed the whole world, are made to breathe again after darkness has been destroyed. May those beams of the thousand-rayed Sun quickly cause everything unwelcome to fall away from you.
